excerpt.verification: Timestamps are on the publisher's player basis, not a file basis: no copies were acquired. Durations read from each video's own player metadata rather than from descriptions, on 2026-07-26. Chapter 1 (H39LNrL_VH0) 7517 s = 2 h 05 m 17 s; chapter 2 (uAn2kSNRLuM) 6115 s = 1 h 41 m 55 s; chapter 3 (Pu-GlIu0Gqo) 4775 s = 1 h 19 m 35 s; chapter 4 (rT5VwYxJbf8) 4975 s = 1 h 22 m 55 s. Total 23382 s = 6 h 29 m 42 s across four files. The goal described these as 'four one-hour chapters'; measured, none is an hour and chapter 1 alone is over two. This manifest carries chapter 1's figures in the source and excerpt fields, with the other three recorded here, because the schema describes one media item. No audio was acquired - the candidate was ruled out on rights before any audio assessment.

recording_conditions.observations: Not assessed. The candidate failed the rights check first and nothing was downloaded or measured, so no claim is made about production values, however evident they may be from the channel's reputation. Reputation is not measurement, and this project prefers benchmark evidence to it. The same caution applies to corpus_tier: polished_professional is a proposed classification from the publisher's reputation, not an assessment, and the schema has no value for 'tier not established'. Read it as where this candidate would sit if it were ever admitted.

truth.notes: None, and none should be added while the rights position stands.

rights.copyright_holder: Oxventure / Outside Xbox Limited; Dungeons & Dragons material remains with Wizards of the Coast
rights.review_notes: None of the four chapters' watch pages carries a Creative Commons licence row in its markup on 2026-07-26, and yt-dlp reports no license field for any of them, so all four are under the Standard YouTube Licence, which grants no download or reproduction right. The detection was controlled against videos that do carry the row, so the absence is a real finding. This is a commercial production by a company that sells its content and runs a membership programme; the material being professionally made and publicly viewable does not make copying it permissible, and a private research use does not create a right the licence withholds. Permission would have to be sought from the rights holder, which is a product-level decision for the user rather than a determination this role can make.

selection.diagnostic_value: Rejected on rights. It would also not have filled the gap it was proposed for: four separately recorded and edited chapters do not test sustained single-file processing, because the breaks, re-setups and edits between them remove precisely the continuity that long-form processing has to survive. What it does offer, and what the corpus still lacks, is campaign-arc continuity across sessions - whether understanding carries from chapter 1 to chapter 4. That property is worth pursuing in a candidate whose licence permits processing; the Mystic Horizon channel publishes a sixteen-episode campaign under CC BY and is the obvious place to look first.
risks: Standard YouTube Licence on all four chapters; no basis to acquire copies.

Chapter count was mistaken for duration in the goal's framing; measured, the four chapters are 6 h 29 m 42 s in total but no single file exceeds 2 h 05 m, so this is a campaign-arc candidate rather than a long-session one.
A commercial rights holder is less likely to grant free research use than a hobbyist creator, so the effort of asking is better spent on the smaller channels.
